lead.headline: Columbia wins twice and takes over first place
lead.deck: The Lions won at Boston University as underdogs and held Saint Peter's to 44. The league went 12-4 this week and covered 11 of 15 lines.
body: Columbia went to Boston University as a 1-point underdog and won 80-71, then came home and beat Saint Peter's 65-44 as a 13.5-point favorite. Josh Pratt led the way in Boston with 18. The Lions are 6-1, first in the power rankings after starting the week second, and 95th nationally in our model at plus-8.6 points per 100 possessions. That makes them the only Ivy team in the top 100, and the gap to second place is nearly seven points.

Penn, the league's preseason pick per the Ivy League's own poll, did its part. The Quakers won 83-73 at La Salle as 2.5-point underdogs, with 20 each from Ethan Lin and Michael Zanoni and a 16-point, 12-rebound, six-assist line from TJ Power. Then Zanoni scored 30 in an 89-74 win over Drexel, a 6-point line Penn cleared by nine. The power rankings still slid them from first to third. Two wins, down two spots. Tough room.

Cornell made the biggest jump, from fifth to second. The Big Red won 84-63 at Morgan State as 6-point favorites and beat Bucknell 92-71 as 11.5-point favorites, with Mateen Rafiq scoring 20 and Jacob Beccles 17. Both lines covered with room to spare.

Princeton went 2-0 and the second win was the best road result in the league. The Tigers beat Monmouth 75-64 behind Christopher Kirkpatrick's 22, then won 79-72 at Liberty as 3.5-point underdogs. Jackson Hicke had 15 points and seven assists there. Liberty is 127th in our model, which is better than every Ivy team but Columbia.

The 12-4 week had two dents. Harvard lost 81-72 at home to Boston University as a 6-point favorite, and Dartmouth lost 67-65 at home to Holy Cross as a 12-point favorite, five days after Harvard won at Holy Cross by 12. The CAA comes calling next: Princeton at UNC Wilmington and Towson at Penn, both on Friday.

column.label: Look Ahead
column.title: Three games that will tell us something
body: **Towson at Penn, Friday, 6 p.m.** No line yet. Our model has Penn 143rd and Towson 164th, close enough that home court is the difference. Penn plays again Saturday against Bucknell, the team Cornell just beat by 21.
**Columbia at St. John's, Tuesday, 6:30 p.m.** No line yet. This is the step up the Lions' schedule hasn't had. A 6-1 record and the league's best rating get tested in Queens.

**Princeton at St. Thomas, Saturday, noon.** The back half of a road weekend that starts at UNC Wilmington. Princeton is 182nd in our model, and two road wins in two days would make that number look stale.

notes.headline: Dartmouth's tough night
notes.body: The Big Green were 12-point favorites at home against Holy Cross and lost 67-65. Ernas Valauskas had 16 points, seven rebounds and four assists, and Anton Strelnikov added 15.

notes.headline: Tey Barbour went for 32
notes.body: Harvard's guard scored 32 against Boston University, the best line by an Ivy player this week, in an 81-72 loss. Earlier in the week Thomas Batties II and Jason Singleton had 16 each in a 77-65 win at Holy Cross.

notes.headline: Yale's three-day trip
notes.body: The Bulldogs played three games in three days. They lost 68-60 at Belmont, beat App State 57-50 as 1-point underdogs, then won 72-70 at Wright State as 5-point underdogs. Riley Fox scored 20 in two of them.

notes.headline: Circle it: Princeton at UNC Wilmington
notes.body: Friday, 3 p.m. ET on FloSports. No line posted yet; our model has UNC Wilmington, the CAA's top-rated team, by 6.5.
